{{Quote|And just then, in my head, a vision of my aunt Celly rose as clear as if she were standing in front of me. She smiled. Patience, Leia. Illumination comes like the sunrise. Slowly. Then all at once.|Leia Organa, thinking of her dead aunt|<ref name="CTE">''[[Star Wars Journal: Captive to Evil]]''</ref>}}
'''Celly Organa''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] from [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] and a member of the [[House of Organa/Legends|House of Organa]], one of the most famous and influential [[Noble/Legends|noble]] families of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. One of four children, she was the sister of [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail]], [[Rouge Organa|Rouge]], and [[Tia Organa]]. Although she was born into [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|wealth]] and privilege on an idyllic [[Planet/Legends|planet]], Organa did not remain idle; in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] leading up to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], she served as [[Chairman/Legends|Chairwoman]] of the [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]]. Under her chairmanship, the movement established a new settlement on the site of [[Chianar]], the cornerstone of which was laid in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].

[[19 BBY/Legends|Three years later]], Organa's brother Bail, then [[Senator/Legends|senator]] of the [[Alderaan sector/Legends|Alderaan sector]], decided to adopt a [[Youngling/Legends|baby]] daughter named [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]]. Organa joined him in the upbringing of his adopted offspring. As a tutor, she could not hide her exasperation with her niece's tomboyish nature, but she loved her nonetheless. Ultimately, Leia turned out well and followed in her [[Parent/Legends|father's]] footsteps, succeeding him as senator to the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]]. In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Celly Organa [[Death/Legends|died]] along with most of her compatriots when the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destroyed]] her [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] with a shot from the [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] of the planet-killing [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|Aunt Rouge, Aunt Celly, and Aunt Tia&hellip; Father's sisters. They never stopped trying to turn me into what they called a Proper Princess&mdash;and marry me off to some brainless twerp from one of the other ancient ruling Houses&hellip;|Leia Organa, musing on her girlhood|<ref name="CotJ" />}}
[[File:Alderaan-TOR.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Celly Organa's homeworld, a planet of grasslands and quiet people]]
Celly Organa was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] from [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]],<ref name="CotJ" /> a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] that many considered to be [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] paradise and the heart of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="CSWEAld">{{CSWECite|I|18|Alderaan}}</ref> A [[Noble/Legends|noblewoman]], she was part of the [[Prince/Legends|princely]] [[House of Organa/Legends|House of Organa]],<ref name="CotJ" /> whose origins could be traced as far back as the colonization of Alderaan<ref name="TORcodex">{{TORcite|type=codex|House Organa}}</ref> in [[27,500 BBY]].<ref name="NEC" /> Her [[Parent/Legends|father]], the [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Organa (viceroy)|Organa]],<ref name="DFR">The novel ''[[Dark Force Rising]]'' established that [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa's]] [[Organa (viceroy)|father]] was a [[Viceroy/Legends|viceroy]]. Since Bail and his sisters share their surname according to ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', this article assumes that they had the same father.</ref> had also [[Reproduction/Legends|begotten]] three other [[Youngling/Legends|children]]: [[Tia Organa|Tia]], [[Rouge Organa|Rouge]], and [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor]], his only son.<ref name="CotJ" /> As the offspring of a [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|wealthy]], prominent, and popular noble house,<ref name="TFUG">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Organa enjoyed a privileged and comfortable life from the [[Standard day/Legends|day]] she drew her first breath.<ref name="Wild Space">In the novel ''[[The Clone Wars: Wild Space]]'', the childhood of the scions of [[House of Organa/Legends|House Organa]] was described in such terms by [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]].</ref> When she reached the age of seventeen, she became an [[Age of responsibility|adult]] in the [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] of the [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanian]] law.<ref name="Age of responsibility">''[[Rebel Dawn]]'' established that the "[[age of responsibility]]" on both [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] and [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] was set at seventeen.</ref> Due to her heritage, she was a princess in her own right<ref name="BHambly-mail">{{EmailCite|email=Wookieepedia:Email/Barbara Hambly|creator=[[Barbara Hambly]]|date=2012-11-13}}</ref> and was part of the [[High Court of Alderaan]], which presided over the planet's [[High Council of Alderaan|High Council]].<ref name="High Court" /> Eventually, she started a family of her own.<ref name="TFUG" /> Her only brother, Bail Prestor, went on to become the [[Senator/Legends|representative]] of the [[Alderaan sector/Legends|Alderaan sector]] to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], the Viceroy and [[First Chairman/Legends|First Chairman]] of the [[Alderaan system/Legends|Alderaan system]] and the husband of [[King/Legends|Queen]] [[Breha Organa/Legends|Breha Organa]],<ref name="DbBail">{{DB|character|bailorgana|Organa, Bail}}</ref> née [[House of Antilles|Antilles]].<ref name="DbRaymus">{{DB|character|captainantilles|Antilles, Raymus}}</ref>

[[File:RRM.jpg|thumb|right|150px|The ground-breaking ceremony of the Chianar settlement]]
In the last [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] of the Republic, the number of people living below the poverty line on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] world of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] government, was increasing. In an effort to counter that trend, the [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]]&mdash;or RRM for short&mdash;was founded. When the movement evolved into a resettlement agency, various new branches were established on several planets, and Organa was appointed [[Chairman/Legends|Chairwoman]] of the RRM. In the third [[Standard month/Legends|month]] of the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Alderaan loosened its immigration laws to allow thousands of [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]] to find shelter, and the government donated one hundred [[Hectare/Legends|hectares]] of plains on the site of [[Chianar]] to be transformed into a new village. Organa supervised the construction commencement ceremony and greeted the first five hundred new settlers. The Alderaanian [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomat]] [[Liana Merian/Legends|Liana Merian]] and the former [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] also participated in the ceremony. On that occasion, a [[Journalist/Legends|journalist]] interviewed Organa for an article to be published in the [[HoloNet News Vol. 531 49|forty-ninth issue]] of the [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] [[HoloNet News CoCo District Edition|CoCo District Edition's]] [[HoloNet News Vol. 531|531st volume]]. In the interview, Organa advocated for more solidarity, stating that the worlds still aligned with the Republic had enough room to accommodate the shelterless who had been forced to abandon their home planets.<ref name="HN9N" />

===Bringing up Leia Organa===
{{Quote|A girl can only take so much primping and posturing. I know my father and aunts mean well, but I didn't ask to be the Princess of the Royal House of Alderaan.|Extract from Leia Organa's youth diary|<ref name="TPLD">{{Tales|11|The Princess Leia Diaries}}</ref>}}
Two months after the inauguration of the Chianar settlement, the Republic went to war with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], a separatist movement led by [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] of [[Serenno/Legends|Serenno]]. After the end of the devastating three-year conflict known as the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="NEC" /> the then-senator Bail Organa decided to adopt [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]], the [[Youngling/Legends|baby]] girl of his late colleague [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]. Meanwhile, the former [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] had shown his true colors, [[Declaration of a New Order|carving]] an authoritarian [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] from the corpse of the old Republic and bestowing the title of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] upon himself.<ref name="ROS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Celly Organa and her sisters came to live at the [[Royal Palace of Alderaan/Legends|Royal Palace]] of [[Aldera/Legends|Aldera]] to help their brother raise his foster daughter.<ref name="TPLD" /> By that point, Organa had become a widow, holding the title of dowager.<ref name="Dowager">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']] referred to [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa's]] adopted aunts as "dowagers."</ref>

[[File:Organas.png|thumb|left|170px|Organa and her sisters were devoted to making a "proper lady" out of their niece Leia.]]
The Princess Organa and her sisters were tasked with drilling the young Leia into a respectable, high-ranking lady.<ref name="DbBail" /> However, baby Leia grew into a tomboyish girl with a fiery temperament. Wishing to tame their passionate niece, Organa and her sisters taught her the arcana of court etiquette.<ref name="CotJ" /> Additionally, they hired other tutors, including the strict [[Vesta|Madame Vesta]], the [[Headmaster/Legends|Headmistress]] of the [[Alderaan Select Academy for Young Ladies]].<ref name="TPLD" /> For his part, the Viceroy worked in the shadows, contributing to the foundation of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], a gathering of factions opposed to the tyranny of Palpatine's Empire.<ref name="DbBail" /> The attempt at bridling their adopted niece was not entirely successful; when the ten-year-old princess performed the "[[Dance of the Twi'lek Slave Girl]]" during a performance at the Select Academy, the Organa sisters were collectively appalled.<ref name="TPLD" /> A few years later, they were further disappointed when a teenaged Leia refused to enter the Court marriage market before she could do so as a senator in her own right.<ref name="CotJ" />

As [[Time/Legends|time]] passed, Organa witnessed her niece coming of age and succeeding her father as representative of the Alderaan [[Sector/Legends|sector]] in the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]].<ref name="CotJ" /> In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]],<ref name="BallDate">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']] stated that [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] was eighteen when she attended the levee, and her birthdate was established as [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] in ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> on the occasion of Leia's nomination as senator, Organa, Rouge, and Tia accompanied Leia to an official levee organized by the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] on Coruscant, now renamed Imperial Center. When the young Senator noticed the presence of [[Gemstone/Legends|jeweled]] Imperial concubines and asked about them, Organa took her aside and briefed her about the court's intrigues.<ref name="CotJ" /> Although the three sisters were still bent on marrying Leia off at the time of her first levee, the Princess was secretly going out with young men, although none the dowagers would approve of.<ref name="TFU2">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' novelization]]</ref> Organa and her siblings were also unaware that, years before, Leia had sneaked out with the young noble [[Raal Panteer]] under the cover of the night to swim in the reflecting pools of Aldera, and they had exchanged their first kiss.<ref name="SWE21">[[Empire 21|''Empire'' 21]]</ref>

===A planet's demise===
{{Quote|Millions of lives vaporized. My father, my best friend Winter, my aunts, my teachers, my friends. All gone. An entire civilization vanished from the galaxy in an instant of heat, of light.|Leia Organa|<ref name="CTE" />}}
In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]], one of Palpatine's [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moffs]], chose to demonstrate the full power of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]], a brand-new [[Moon/Legends|moon]]-sized [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] equipped with a planet-destroying [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]]. Since the Empire had grown suspicious of Bail Organa's true allegiance, Tarkin had the entire planet of Alderaan destroyed by the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], with a captive Leia being forced to watch.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> On a warm evening late in the spring, Celly Organa, a proud daughter of the House of Organa, [[Death/Legends|died]] in the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction]] of her [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]],<ref name="CotJ" /> along with more than a billion other beings.<ref name="CCW">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''</ref>

===Legacy===
{{Quote|So I lay down in my bunk, and I thought about Alderaan. I couldn't think about Father or my aunts&mdash;that hurt too much. So I thought about the green fields and the blue flowers, and my favorite walk through the hills.|Leia Organa|<ref name="CTE" />}}
Despite the clear differences of opinion they had on many issues, Leia immediately realized how much she would miss her Aunt Celly, her recommendations, and her annoying riddle games. During one of her first private conversations with the [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooinian]] farm boy [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]&mdash;who was in fact her estranged [[Twin/Legends|twin]] brother&mdash;Leia started daydreaming about her aunt advising her to be patient like she used to.<ref name="CTE" /> Even [[16 ABY/Legends|sixteen years later]], when Leia had become the [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]] of a democratic [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], she remembered her conversation with her aunt on the Imperial Court's intrigues while meeting again with [[Roganda Ismaren/Legends|Roganda Ismaren]], a former concubine of the Emperor.<ref name="CotJ" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Coruscant's getting even more crowded each day. There's plenty of elbow room in the Republic, as long as worlds are willing to share.|Celly Organa, Chairwoman of the Alderaanian RRM|<ref name="HN9N" />}}
In her last years, Celly Organa was a plump woman with a pink face.<ref name="CotJ" /> As was customary among Alderaanian adults,<ref name="TCS">''[[The Crystal Star]]''</ref> she had long [[Hair/Legends|hair]] that she would decorate with cut [[Plant/Legends|flowers]].<ref name="TPLD" /> When her niece Leia first attended the Emperor's reception, Organa's hair was fading with age, but she would still display complicated&mdash;and somewhat antiquated&mdash;hairstyles that included twirls, pearls, and small garlands.<ref name="CotJ" />

Although she was born into luxury and prosperity, with her family's wealth seemingly limitless,<ref name="TFUG" /> Organa had genuine concerns for those most in need. At the time she presided over the RRM, she publicly stated there was enough space in the Republic for everyone to live decently, on the condition that everyone agreed to share.<ref name="HN9N" /> Organa shared many things with her sisters, including a taste for iridescent earrings made from [[Old Republic bronze]]<ref name="CotJ" /> and her pleading for patience and reflection.<ref name="CTE" /> Beside her undoubted qualities, she was also known for her personality quirks, such as indulging daily outbreaks of hypochondria&mdash;during which she would lie down in her chambers<ref name="CotJ" />&mdash;and making riddles, a habit that usually greatly annoyed her niece.<ref name="CTE" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|It always bothered me slightly that in the original Star Wars (and I think of the films by their original titles), Leia sees her home&mdash;all her family, the place she grew up, everyone she knows&mdash;destroyed before her eyes, and then we just go on to the next thing. Who WERE these people that she lost? Who were her family?|Barbara Hambly|<ref name="BHambly-mail" />}}
[[File:ChildrenoftheJedi-Paperback.png|thumb|right|150px|Celly Organa was first mentioned in Barbara Hambly's ''Children of the Jedi''.]]
Celly Organa was first mentioned along with her sisters in [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], a [[1995]] novel written by [[Barbara Hambly]] and published by [[Bantam Spectra]]. In that book, the Organa sisters were introduced as the main caretakers of a teenaged Leia Organa.<ref name="CotJ" /> However, in the [[1981]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] [[Star Wars (1977) 53|''The Last Gift From Alderaan!'']], the fifty-third issue of the [[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'']] series by [[Marvel Comics]], Princess Leia wondered whether her father was alone or "with mother" when Alderaan was destroyed. That statement suggested that Breha Organa had remained alive until the very end of Alderaan.<ref name="LGFA">[[Star Wars (1977) 53|''Star Wars'' (1977) 53]]</ref> Yet, the Marvel series was deemed "[[Canon|Secondary Canon]]," which could be overridden or [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] by newer licensed sources considered "Continuity Canon."<ref name="FBChee">{{Facebook|noprofile=1|url=notes/keeper-of-the-holocron/whatd-i-say-again-select-posts-by-me-regarding-continuity/201910849829849|author=[[Leland Chee]]|date=2011-04-06|quote=There is a secondary 'S' continuity classification used for older published materials created when there was less attention to making everything in the Expanded Universe fit with everything else in the EU.|nobackup=1}}</ref> While prominent [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] sources like ''Children of the Jedi'' established that the Organa sisters tutored their niece in the absence of a mother,<ref name="CotJ" /> the ''[[2013 Topps Star Wars Illustrated: A New Hope]]'' trading card set released by [[Topps]] in [[2013]] showed that Queen Breha had indeed survived until the destruction of Alderaan.<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=2013 Topps Star Wars Illustrated: A New Hope|cardname=The Destruction of Alderaan|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/87473/cid/6296533/2013-Topps-Star-Wars-Illustrated-A-New-Hope-66-The-Destruction-of-Alderaan}}</ref>

When she saw [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], Barbara Hambly was bothered by the rapidity with which the destruction of Alderaan was set aside. With the explosion of her homeworld, Princess Leia had lost everyone she knew and loved, but the action pressed on to the next part of the story. Hambly sought to put a human face on the Princess' grief, which prompted her to create new family members. The author came up with a group of aunts, since royal sisters would have been much more likely to stay close to the court than Bail Organa's potential brothers. Hambly also stated that, had her aunts survived the destruction of Alderaan, Leia Organa would have gotten to know them much better, learning to value each for her qualities.<ref name="BHambly-mail" />

Celly Organa was specifically mentioned by name five times throughout the narrative, which makes her the second most cited of Leia's aunts, the first one being Rouge.<ref name="CotJ" /> Hambly envisioned her as the "classic middle child," older than Tia and younger than Rouge. In creating her character, she sought to portray her as sweet-natured and understanding. At the time of Leia's upbringing, her Aunt Celly was single, "either through widowhood, possibly [[Divorce/Legends|divorce]], or her own choice."<ref name="BHambly-mail" />

In [[2002]], "Celly Organa" was erroneously mentioned as Alderaan's [[Minister of Education/Legends|Minister of Education]] and Bail Organa's wife in [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 67|sixty-seventh issue]] of ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]''.<ref name="FF67">{{FactFile|67|ORG 1-2|Bail Organa}}</ref> At the time ''The Official Fact File'' was published, [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] had not been released yet, and the character of Breha Organa, née Antilles, had not yet been created.<ref name="ROS" /> The same year, Bail Organa's sisters made their first pictorial appearance in "[[The Princess Leia Diaries]]," a short comic from the ''[[Star Wars Tales]]'' series that was written by [[Jason Hall]] and illustrated by [[Chris Brunner]]. Although the three aunts went nameless in the comic, only one matches<ref name="TPLD" /> the description of Organa as fair-haired.<ref name="CotJ" />

The [[2010]] reference book ''[[Star Wars Blueprints: Rebel Edition]]'', written by [[Ryder Windham]], stated that the late [[Mazicia Organa]], Queen of Alderaan more than a decade before the Clone Wars, was Bail Organa's mother.<ref name="SWBRE">''[[Star Wars Blueprints: Rebel Edition]]''</ref> However, whether she was also the mother of his sisters was never clarified.
